hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with hematuria, flank pain, hypertension, and palpable bilateral flank masses. Family history of ADPKD (autosomal dominant — 50% of children inherit). ADPKD is the most common inherited kidney disease — mutations in PKD1 (85%, chromosome 16) or PKD2 (15%, chromosome 4). Cysts develop in kidneys (and liver, pancreas) over decades, eventually causing renal failure by age 50-60. Diagnosis: renal ultrasound — multiple bilateral cysts in enlarged kidneys (usually by age 30 for PKD1). CT/MRI for more detail. Labs: elevated Cr (declining renal function), UA shows hematuria. Screen for cerebral aneurysms (berry aneurysms — 5-10% of ADPKD patients, higher if family history) with MRA/CTA brain. Management: BP control with ACEI/ARB (nephroprotective), treat UTIs aggressively, avoid contact sports (cyst rupture risk). Tolvaptan (vasopressin antagonist) slows cyst growth. Genetic counseling.
